subject: Early-payment discount accrual + invoice split causing AR suspense postings
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-07-12 09:12 PDT
Subject: Early-payment discount accrual + invoice split causing AR suspense postings

Team — quick heads-up. During the month-end AR review I noticed a cluster of CloudSail payments that hit the suspense account instead of being applied to the aged invoices. The root cause appears to be a combination of: (1) our new split-invoice flow (we issue a micro-refund when a billing period boundary overlaps a partial-period credit) and (2) the early-payment discount (EPD) logic applying on the payment run rather than at invoice level, which changes the allocation.

Attached is a CSV extract from the July 1 payment run and a PDF snapshot of the suspense ledger showing ~12 items (~$27k) that look like they should have applied to open invoices but are currently in 1200-Suspense. If we don't clear these before close, revenue recognition for July will be off because some of the invoices were already recognized in June under the split flow.

Can Lauren/Ben weigh in on whether we should: (A) post a reversing JE to move the suspense amounts back to AR and then reapply against the invoices, or (B) treat as a July adjustment and post to the EPD accrual account and then true-up in Aug? Grace — can you check whether CloudSail submitted any special payment instructions that would cause the payment processor to tag these as 'refunds' instead of 'payments'? I'm looping Alicia to confirm on their side.

Action request: Please review attachments by end of day 7/12 and reply with preferred remediation path. If we need a JE, I'll draft the template for AP/GL.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cloudsail_payment_run_2028-07-01.csv (CSV stub), suspense_ledger_snapshot_July2028.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia@cloudsail.com>
Date: 2028-07-12 11:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Early-payment discount accrual + invoice split causing AR suspense postings

Marcus — I pulled the CloudSail payment run and spoke briefly with their billing ops. They confirm the payment was a consolidated ACH covering three invoice IDs, but their payment metadata included a 'refund_flag=true' for the micro-refund we issue when their billing cycle overlaps a previous period. Their processor (StripeConnect via their gateway) is tagging that line as a refund which our upload script currently maps to the Suspense bucket.

Alicia: can you ask your billing team to remove the refund flag for that line in future runs? For today, they said they can re-emit a corrected payment file if we want (they can backfill as well).

Lauren/Ben — given this is a tagging issue on the payment file, I think option (A) is cleaner: move the items from Suspense back to AR, reapply to the invoices, and then separately post the EPD accrual for the discount amount at invoice level so revenue recognition lines up. That keeps the original revenue entries intact. If PwC is going to look at July close, I'd prefer we avoid hitting an accrual account if we can reapply cleanly.

Grace
Finance Manager, Customer Accounting

Thanks Grace and Marcus. I agree with (A) as the remediation — reclass suspense -> AR, reapply payments, then post a separate EPD accrual at the invoice level so revenue recognition remains consistent.

I'll prepare a JE template for the reversal + reapplication and include a short audit memo that documents: why the amounts were posted to suspense, how we identified the correct invoices, and the control steps to prevent recurrence (update the payment ingestion mapping and require a 'transaction_type' in their flat file). Tagging PwC for visibility — see their note below in case they need documentation for interim testing.

Ben, can you validate: (1) whether the invoice amounts were recognized in June (I saw some entries around 2028-06-29 in RevMap), and (2) whether we have remaining unapplied credits on the account after reapply that would change revenue deferrals? If either answer is yes, we need the JE and memo before close.

Lauren
Accounting Lead, Revenue Recognition

Confirmed: I pulled the RevMap entries. Three of the affected invoice lines were recognized in June (rev entry dates 2028-06-29) because of the split-invoice recognition rule we applied for mid-period proration. That means if we post the suspense->AR reclassification and reapply payments now, we will indeed have to post a matching reversing JE to remove the premature recognition or file a July adjusting entry depending on the customer's cutover choice.

My suggested sequence:
1) Grace to confirm corrected payment file from CloudSail (or we accept the re-emit).
2) Lauren to prepare JE template: (A) suspense->AR reclass; (B) if reapply creates a mismatch to recognized revenue, prepare the revenue reversal JE with explanation.
3) Marcus to approve the JE and memo for executives & PwC.

I've drafted a proposed_JE_reclass_template.xlsx (attached) — includes the debit/credit lines and proposed GL accounts. If we want to avoid altering recognized revenue in July, CloudSail can opt to have us book the movement as an AR reapply and then do a one-line July deferral true-up; I'd prefer clean reclassification + revenue reversal to preserve audit trail.

Ben
Senior Accounting Analyst
